comparison: Both strongly support the characterization of zebrafish Ctla-4 homolog (C43-C54). OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary approaches including database searches, alignments, phylogenetic analysis, Western blots, and expression profiling. Peer reviewers praised the comprehensive characterization with no concerns raised. Peer result additionally includes C4 and C38, while OpenEval R1 does not include C38 (which appears in OpenEval R2).

Both support the generation and basic phenotypic characterization of the mutant (C55-C59). OpenEval includes C38-C39 while peer includes only C39. Both note genotyping, Western blot confirmation, and quantitative measurements. Peer reviewers unanimously praised the thorough characterization with no concerns. OpenEval specifically highlights the survival advantage of this model over mammalian systems.

Both strongly support histological findings (C60-C75, C40). OpenEval emphasizes multiple histological techniques and TEM with appropriate statistical comparisons. Peer reviewers found evidence 'very strong' with comprehensive demonstration of IBD-like phenotype. Peer result additionally includes C5-C7 not in OpenEval R3. Reviewer 4 had minor concerns about PAS quantification but did not challenge overall findings.

Perfect agreement on transcriptomic analysis claims (C76-C88, C8). Both support RNA-seq findings with appropriate validation. OpenEval highlights statistical thresholds, RT-qPCR validation, PPI network analysis, and MPO assays. Peer reviewers praised comprehensive transcriptomic analysis providing mechanistic insight. Reviewer 4 had minor concern about figure size but did not question data quality.

Perfect agreement on scRNA-seq analysis of enterocytes (C89-C94). Both support findings of increased apoptosis and downregulation of junction genes. OpenEval notes appropriate quality control and internal consistency with ultrastructural findings. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of comprehensive characterization supporting immune system homeostasis disruption.

Perfect agreement on immune cell composition changes (C95-C101, C9-C11). Both support scRNA-seq sub-clustering findings. OpenEval notes the unique Th2 subset and decreased ILC3 population, suggesting functional validation would be beneficial. Peer Reviewer 2 initially noted concerns about composition vs. number of immune cells but later stated concerns were sufficiently addressed.

Perfect agreement on microbiome findings (C104-C115, C12-C13). Both support 16S rRNA gene sequencing results showing altered diversity and composition. OpenEval notes modest sample size and inability to determine causality vs. consequence. Peer reviewers supported findings with Reviewer 4 having minor terminology comment but not challenging data. Both note consistency with mammalian IBD patterns.

Perfect agreement on mechanistic findings (C116-C124, C41). Both support multiple complementary approaches including functional assays, structural predictions, Co-IP, and MST. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative binding affinity measurements and internal consistency. Peer Reviewer 2 initially found explanation oversimplified regarding lymphocyte proliferation vs. composition changes but later stated concerns were sufficiently addressed.

Perfect agreement on rescue experiments (C125-C129, C15). Both strongly support therapeutic potential of soluble Ctla-4-Ig treatment. OpenEval notes appropriate controls and consistency across multiple readouts but indicates mechanism of action and long-term effects need further elucidation. Peer reviewers enthusiastically supported findings, noting exciting therapeutic potential and additional mechanistic insights.

Strong agreement on integrative conclusions (C14, C16-C18, C42). Both support establishment of zebrafish as IBD model. OpenEval includes C40 not in peer result, and peer includes C40 in different context. OpenEval tempers claim about CTLA-4 link to human IBD, noting model demonstrates sufficiency but human causality remains correlative. Peer reviewers unanimously praised the model as 'key study with convincing evidence' and valuable substitution for mouse models.

Both support background and literature claims (C1-C3, C19-C37). OpenEval notes these are appropriately cited contextual claims establishing knowledge gap and justifying zebrafish approach. Peer result includes additional literature claims (C102-C103, C130-C138) that OpenEval addresses separately in R12. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted background by not challenging it and noting manuscript was well organized.

OpenEval R12 addresses literature claims about translational relevance (C102-C103, C130-C138) that demonstrate parallels with mammalian IBD. These claims appear in peer R11 along with introductory background claims. Both note these are appropriately cited contextual statements, not original findings. OpenEval emphasizes these strengthen translational relevance of the model.
